name: How to Plan a Custom Bathroom Storage Layout That Fits Your Wall Space
description: Measure total wall dimensions, ceiling height, and the exact swing arc of the entry door, shower enclosure, and vanity drawers. Confirm that opening a storage cabinet will never strike adjacent glass

step.name: Step 1: Take precise room measurements and map clear door swings
step.text: Measure total wall dimensions, ceiling height, and the exact swing arc of the entry door, shower enclosure, and vanity drawers. Confirm that opening a storage cabinet will never strike adjacent glass or block entry clearance into the room.

step.name: Step 2: Locate concealed plumbing stacks, vents, and electrical runs
step.text: Use a stud finder and inspect adjoining rooms or basement chases to determine what runs through your target walls. Deep built-ins and recessed cubbies cannot share wall space with main vent stacks or primary supply lines without rerouting those services.

step.name: Step 3: Select moisture-tolerant cabinet materials and corrosion-resistant hardware
step.text: Choose solid wood, high-density moisture-resistant core materials, and factory-sealed finishes designed for humid bathroom conditions. Ensure hinges, slides, and shelf pins feature corrosion-resistant plating so they do not rust from daily shower steam.

step.name: Step 4: Open wall framing and install structural horizontal blocking
step.text: Expose the wall studs where the storage unit will sit and install solid two-by-four wood blocking between studs. Heavy hanging cabinets and floating tall units need structural wood backing rather than basic hollow-wall drywall anchors to safely hold heavy stacks of towels and toiletries.

step.name: Step 5: Position, level, and securely fasten the cabinetry
step.text: Lift the storage unit into position, confirm plumb and level with a precision spirit level, and drive rated cabinet screws directly into your solid blocking. Check that the cabinet box remains perfectly square so doors hang true and latch effortlessly.

step.name: Step 6: Seal all wall penetrations and install interior fixtures
step.text: Apply paintable silicone sealant around cabinet perimeters to keep stray splash water from seeping behind the woodwork. Adjust internal shelving, install soft-close hinges, and verify that plumbing shutoff valves remain completely unobstructed. If your layout requires opening load-bearing walls or moving supply pipes, hiring a licensed builder keeps your project smooth and compliant.
